# formal_native_user_v3 (Resource)

A Native User the Formal connector authenticates to a Resource as. The Resource decides which Native User a session uses through its `formal_resource_native_user_selection` expression.

## Example Usage

```terraform
resource "formal_resource" "db" {
  name       = "analytics-postgres"
  hostname   = "analytics.internal"
  technology = "postgres"
  port       = 5432

  native_users_v3_enabled = true
}

# Username and password, read from an environment variable on the connector.
resource "formal_native_user_v3" "basic" {
  resource_id = formal_resource.db.id
  label       = "admin"

  basic {
    username = "app_admin"
    password {
      environment_variable = "ANALYTICS_ADMIN_PASSWORD"
    }
  }
}

# AWS IAM, inheriting the role from the connector's environment.
resource "formal_native_user_v3" "aws_iam" {
  resource_id = formal_resource.db.id
  label       = "iam"

  aws_iam {
    username = "app_iam"
  }
}

resource "formal_resource" "api" {
  name       = "billing-api"
  hostname   = "billing.internal"
  technology = "http"
  port       = 443

  native_users_v3_enabled = true
}

resource "formal_native_user_v3" "bearer_token" {
  resource_id = formal_resource.api.id
  label       = "service-account"

  http_bearer {
    header = "Authorization"
    token {
      environment_variable = "BILLING_API_TOKEN"
    }
  }
}

# Credentials resolved at connection time by a hook running on the connector,
# for example to mint short-lived credentials from a secrets manager.
resource "formal_native_user_v3" "from_hook" {
  resource_id = formal_resource.db.id
  label       = "dynamic"

  hook {
    output_type               = "basic"
    allowlisted_env_variables = ["FORMAL_ENV_USER", "FORMAL_ENV_PASSWORD"]
    code                      = <<-TYPESCRIPT
      export default async function (_input, env) {
        return {
          username: env.FORMAL_ENV_USER,
          password: env.FORMAL_ENV_PASSWORD,
        };
      }
    TYPESCRIPT
  }
}
```

## Schema

### Required

- `label` (String) A name for this Native User, unique within the Resource. Selection expressions reference the Native User by ID, so the label is safe to rename.
- `resource_id` (String) The ID of the Resource this Native User authenticates to.

### Optional

- `aws_iam` (Block List, Max: 1) AWS IAM authentication. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedblock--aws_iam))
- `aws_iam_role` (Block List, Max: 1) AWS IAM authentication using an assumed role. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedblock--aws_iam_role))
- `azure_iam` (Block List, Max: 1) Azure IAM authentication. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedblock--azure_iam))
- `basic` (Block List, Max: 1) Username and password authentication, for example Postgres or MySQL. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedblock--basic))
- `gcp_iam` (Block List, Max: 1) GCP IAM authentication. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedblock--gcp_iam))
- `hook` (Block List, Max: 1) Credentials resolved on the connector by running a hook. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedblock--hook))
- `http_api_key_header` (Block List, Max: 1) HTTP API key authentication, sent as a header. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedblock--http_api_key_header))
- `http_api_key_query` (Block List, Max: 1) HTTP API key authentication, sent as a query parameter. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedblock--http_api_key_query))
- `http_basic` (Block List, Max: 1) HTTP Basic authentication, injected on a named header. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedblock--http_basic))
- `http_bearer` (Block List, Max: 1) HTTP Bearer token authentication, injected on a named header. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedblock--http_bearer))
- `kubernetes_inline` (Block List, Max: 1) Kubernetes authentication using an inline kubeconfig document. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedblock--kubernetes_inline))
- `kubernetes_path` (Block List, Max: 1) Kubernetes authentication using a kubeconfig file path on the connector. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedblock--kubernetes_path))
- `snowflake_key` (Block List, Max: 1) Snowflake key-pair authentication. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedblock--snowflake_key))
- `ssh_key` (Block List, Max: 1) SSH private key authentication. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedblock--ssh_key))
- `termination_protection` (Boolean) If set to true, this Native User cannot be deleted.

### Read-Only

- `created_at` (String) Creation time of the Native User.
- `id` (String) The ID of the Native User.
- `updated_at` (String) Last update time of the Native User.

- `allowlisted_network_hosts` (List of String) Network hosts the hook may access.
